neighbours.label: The idioms 'none of X's business', 'mind your own business' and 'who am I to'
fire: Honestly, how she spends her money is none of my business.
Tell him that what I do on weekends is none of his business.
We think their divorce is none of our business, so we stay out.
Stop asking about my salary, because it is none of your business.
If you don't like it, then just mind your own business and move along.
Neighbors should learn to mind their own business about the fence.
He drinks too much, but then who am I to judge him?
She chose a strange path, yet who are we to criticize?
quiet: Honestly, how she spends her money is a mystery to my family.
Tell him that what I do on weekends is running my own business.
We think their shop is a big business, so we invest.
Stop asking about my brother, because none of his friends know him.
If you don't like it, then just open your own business and move along.
Neighbors should learn to mend their own side of the fence.
He drinks too much, so who am I calling to drive him home?
She chose a strange path, so who are we following now?

predictions: The idioms fire at ' business' or ' to'; literal business, 'none of' with other nouns and 'who am I' with other verbs stay quiet.
short: none of my business, who am I to
